texts: good. the query puts the unknown in the individual slot of the fused role-title kind chief_keeper — exactly the atom a matching statement ("X is the chief Keeper") stores — and the answer comes back bare, unbound by any name.
What hunts nightmoths at a lantern-row?

good. the hunter is the bare wh-answer in the hunting event's agent slot, the prey stays a kind-level object the hunting does not change, and the lantern-row binds by its kind in the location slot with no tense atom, which is right for the generic present.

mixed: the count line is the most the instruction set licenses and it does bind a stated count ("three Keepers are active"), but a plural's copular property is normally stored per member ("the Keepers are active") or as a vague count phrase ("several Keepers are active"), and neither leaves a number sitting on the group for this query to read — so the how-many form will usually come back empty. Ask for the Keepers themselves and read the count off the answers: "Which Keepers are active?"
What lies under the water in the Sunken Cove?

good. "lies" states a position rather than an event, so the thing asked for sits in the unknown slot of an entity-attached "under" atom over the water, and the Sunken Cove binds by its name as what contains that water — the same attachment a statement worded this way would take.
Where does the cold-threshold wind come from?

good. the wind binds by its compound kind, the asked-for origin is the bare unknown in the coming event's source slot, and the wind is the undergoer of the motion rather than a volitional doer, which is the reading a natural force takes.
Why do the lanterns of Aelmere burn every night?

good. the query asks for the reason of the burning itself, keeps the habitual reading of "every night" (a night slot plus its daily cycle, no tense), and binds both the lantern group and its Aelmere link.
Why does a Keeper store the mire-essence that forms in the cauldron?
good. the storing is the focus event the reason is asked of, and "that forms in the cauldron" comes through as its own forming event with the mire-essence and the cauldron both in place.
Why does the Council redistribute mire-essence reserves?
good. the query asks why the redistributing happens, with the Council as the doer and the mire-essence reserves as what is moved, and it adds nothing the question did not ask.
Why did the thread harvest at the West Row fall in Year 1?

mixed: nothing is lost and the query does ask for the reason of the fall, but the wording leaves two things to chance — "fall" reads either as a drop in yield or as "took place in Year 1", and a place phrase hung on the harvest noun ("the thread harvest at the West Row") has no settled encoding, so the row link is recorded here in a different shape from your parallel Middle Row question and the two will not match each other. If you mean the yield dropped, write "Why did the West Row thread harvest decline in Year 1?"; if you mean the harvest was held then, write "Why did the West Row thread harvest take place in Year 1?" — the named premodifier gives the row one fixed encoding either way.
Why did the thread harvest at the Middle Row fall on day 17 of Year 1?

bad: "fall on day 17 of Year 1" was taken literally — the query invents a separate falling event with the harvest as its object and puts the date on that falling, so it asks the reason for a fall rather than the reason the harvest was on day 17. Date the harvest with a plain light verb instead: "Why did the thread harvest at the Middle Row take place on day 17 of Year 1?" If you actually meant the yield dropped that day, say so with an unambiguous verb: "Why did the thread harvest at the Middle Row decline on day 17 of Year 1?"
Why does a surviving nightmoth flee to a dim lantern in the Hollows?

good. the query asks for the reason of the fleeing itself, keeps "surviving" and "dim" as plain descriptions of the moth and the lantern, uses the goal sense of "to" for a lantern it flees toward, and binds "Hollows" by its name alone. The reviewer's worry that "in the Hollows" might belong to the lantern rather than to the fleeing was judged not a defect — both attachments are licensed and the question is asked faithfully either way — so no rewrite is needed.
Why did the Council discuss the sky-cat drought in Year 1?

good. the query asks for the reason of the Council's discussing, keeps the sky-cat drought as the thing discussed (unchanged by being discussed), and pins the discussion to Year 1 in the past, so every part of the question is carried.
Why does the Council meet at the Watch?

good. the query asks for the reason of the Council's meeting, treats the Council as one body doing the meeting rather than as separate members, and puts "at the Watch" on the meeting itself; the unmarked present is read as a standing practice, which is what the question intends.
Why does Old Vesh remember two bad winters?

good. Old Vesh is found by name, remembering is treated as a state he is in with the winters as what he remembers, and "two bad winters" keeps the count of two on the pair while "bad" is said of each winter separately — the same shape a statement of the same content would take.
good. "the moon" becomes one specific thing of its kind and "full" is stated of that thing directly, with no extra tense or hedging — exactly what the sentence asserts.

good. the query leaves the action open and asks for whatever the Council is the doer of, so any stored Council activity will answer it; the moon fact from the first sentence names no referent of this question, so nothing from it is pulled in or repeated.
